phases.name: Phase 1: The Nervous System
phases.description: Define the substrate, then build the core data structures and loop driver

features.name: Brainstem / Project Lifecycle
features.description: Recursive rhythm pattern: prepare → execute → integrate → gate at every scale
features.plan: Define the end-to-end project lifecycle that the Attention Scheduler will drive. Not implementation — design specification. What happens at each beat, which components fire, what data flows.
features.notes: The brainstem has three responsibilities, not one. (1) RHYTHM: recursive four-phase pattern (prepare/execute/integrate/gate) that nests at every scale. Each phase maps to a brain region. (2) HOMEOSTASIS: continuous monitoring of vital signs (WM load, prediction accuracy, context capacity, learning health, weight volatility) with reflex-level responses. Context management is breathing — evict/load without PFC involvement. (3) REST: load-triggered consolidation cycles (NE=0) using the same rhythm pattern. Crystallize episodes, prune memory, decay connections, recalibrate predictions, settle weights. Rest happens when the system needs it, not on a schedule.

features.name: Peripheral Nervous System / I/O Boundary
features.description: What the system can perceive (afferent) and do (efferent) in the world
features.plan: Define the I/O surface. Motor Cortex produces intentions, PNS translates to tool calls. Decouple cognition from specific tool implementations.
features.notes: Design: Option B (structured intentions) with Option A implementation (Agent SDK tools under the hood). Intention type has dual layers: semantic (Cerebellum/Hippocampus/BG) + structural (PNS execution). Checkpoint gate modulated by Norepinephrine + Cerebellum confidence — first load-bearing use of neurotransmitter signals. Perception type handles both efferent responses and unsolicited afferent signals. Phase 2 wires real tool execution.

features.name: Working Memory
features.description: Real data structure — patterns, scores, decisions, conventions across tasks
features.plan: Replace the local variables in orchestrator.ts with a proper WorkingMemory class that persists across tasks. Must hold: task graph, established patterns, score trends, key decisions, inhibited senses list, and open questions.
features.notes: Redesigned: dual-level score tracking (receptor-level ground truth + sense-level aggregation on demand). Self-describing ScoreEntry with activationPath — no SensoryCortex dependency. Patterns are minimal freeform strings (detection mechanism left to emerge). InhibitedSense tracks source + reason (for Thalamus explanation and Amygdala override). OpenQuestion type for escalation. Full WorkingMemoryState is serializable via structuredClone snapshot(). Score trends use split-halves algorithm with 0.5 threshold. Sense trends aggregate per-task receptor means to prevent high-receptor-count senses from dominating. getLoad() preserved as brainstem vital sign. See diagrams/working-memory-connections.mmd for full system connection map.

subtasks.detail: src/types/working-memory.ts — ScoreEntry (receptor + activationPath + score), ScoreSnapshot, ScoreTrend (receptor or sense level), WMTask + TaskSummary, EstablishedPattern (minimal), OpenQuestion, InhibitedSense (with source tracking), WorkingMemoryState

subtasks.detail: WM threaded through entire factory chain: Cortex → Brainstem → project → task-dispatch → sensory-cortex → build-cycle. task-dispatch.prepare: registers graph tasks via wm.addTask(). task-dispatch.execute: wm.startTask() before dispatch. build-cycle.integrate: wm.recordScores() each cycle. sensory-cortex.integrate: wm.completeTask() with full result. task-dispatch.integrate: homeostasis.update('workingMemoryLoad', wm.getLoad()) + wm.failTask() on escalation. completeTask skips score recording if build-cycle already recorded. Trend computation deduplicates by taskId (last snapshot wins). Cortex.run() handles addTask/startTask for single-task path. 38/38 smoke tests still passing.

features.name: Thalamus
features.description: Context routing layer — each consumer gets exactly what it needs
features.plan: Build the central relay that assembles context for each consumer. Dual-layer API: Layer 1 categorical getters (stable, any consumer composes from these) + Layer 2 convenience composers (encode selection intelligence for known consumers). Key principle: contextual extraction, not concatenation. Generous inclusion with clear organization for v1 — filter more aggressively later once we see what the system actually uses.
features.notes: Brainstem owns the Thalamus (same pattern as WM and HomeostasisMonitor). Constructed with persistent sources (WM, PNS), updated with per-project sources (intent, taste) when a run starts. Passed to rhythm definition factories. Future sources (hippocampus, cerebellum, basal ganglia) plug in via optional fields — no registration ceremony. Taste dissolution and intent slicing are future enhancements once the routing infrastructure exists.

subtasks.name: Wire NE modulation of briefing depth
subtasks.detail: Phase 4. Scheduler produces neLevel per task. Thalamus consumes it to modulate extraction depth: high NE → more patterns, more trend detail, more decision history. Low NE → lean briefings, essentials only. Requires: Norepinephrine signal (#22) to be real. The neLevel is already threaded through SensoryCortexContext — Thalamus just needs to read it.

subtasks.name: Wire explore/exploit mode into briefing framing
subtasks.detail: Phase 4. Scheduler determines explore vs exploit per task. Thalamus responds: exploit → emphasize established patterns, highlight what's working, constrain toward proven approaches. Explore → de-emphasize patterns, surface open questions, frame capabilities as possibilities. Same WM data, different emphasis. Requires: Basal Ganglia (#16) or Explore Phase (#10) to make mode meaningful.

subtasks.name: Build forEscalation() convenience composer
subtasks.detail: Phase 5. When the Scheduler escalates, Thalamus assembles rich human-facing context: which trends are declining, what was tried, what patterns exist, what decisions led here, what questions are open. Semantic enrichment for the human consumer — not just 'scores are cratering' but the full picture. Requires: Escalation Pathways (#23).

subtasks.name: Wire taste dissolution into briefings
subtasks.detail: Future. LLM-powered contextual rewriting of taste per consumer. The founding conversation's breakthrough: 'the taste profile is a source the distiller draws from, never a document the agent reads.' Currently taste is passed as structured fields. Dissolution would rewrite it into task-specific natural language guidance. Requires: the routing infrastructure (done) + an LLM call in the Thalamus's convenience composers.

subtasks.name: Wire Hippocampus as Thalamus source
subtasks.detail: Phase 3. Add hippocampus to ThalamusSources. getAccumulatedContext() and getHistoricalContext() (new getter) include relevant episodes and crystallized principles. forConsultation/forMotor enrichment gains episode context. Requires: Hippocampus (#14) + Crystallization (#15).

subtasks.name: Wire Cerebellum predictions as Thalamus source
subtasks.detail: Phase 3. Add cerebellum to ThalamusSources. New getPredictiveContext() getter. forMotor enrichment includes 'the system predicts these scores — adjust accordingly.' forEvaluation enrichment includes predicted vs actual for this receptor. Requires: Cerebellum (#18).

features.name: Attention Scheduler
features.description: Stateless decision function — reads signals, returns one action. Replaces naive nextReadyTask() in task-dispatch.prepare().
features.plan: Not a loop driver (brainstem handles that). A stateless decision function called by task-dispatch.prepare(). Reads WM, task graph, vitals. Returns: dispatch-task (with NE + mode), escalate, rest, replan, or complete. Priority cascade: complete > perseveration > drift-replan > drift-escalate > open-questions > cratering > rest > dispatch > deadlock. Extensible for future signals via optional fields on SchedulerSignals.

subtasks.detail: src/types/attention-scheduler.ts — SchedulerAction (5 variants: dispatch-task, escalate, rest, replan, complete), SchedulerSignals (WM snapshot + vitals + optional drift/perseverating/prospectiveTriggers/routineMatches), SchedulerConfig + DEFAULT_SCHEDULER_CONFIG

subtasks.name: Wire NE + mode to Thalamus briefing modulation
subtasks.detail: Phase 4. neLevel and mode already flow through SensoryCortexContext.briefing but Thalamus doesn't read them. Higher NE → richer briefings (more patterns, more context). Explore mode → de-emphasize patterns, surface capability range. Exploit → emphasize what's working, constrain the builder. Requires: Norepinephrine (#22).

subtasks.name: Wire replan action to Planner
subtasks.detail: Phase 5. Scheduler returns 'replan' but it currently surfaces as GateEscalate to the human. When Planner exists, project rhythm gate should catch replan escalations (context.type === 'replan-request') and re-invoke Planner to re-decompose. Requires: Planner (#1).

subtasks.name: Wire escalation resume flow
subtasks.detail: Phase 5. When Scheduler escalates and human responds, system needs to resume from where it paused. Depends on brainstem's pause/resume wire (runner.ts pausedAt snapshot + re-entry). Human answer should resolve open questions in WM, then Scheduler re-evaluates. Requires: Escalation Pathways (#23) + brainstem pause/resume wire.

subtasks.name: Make task selection weights plastic
subtasks.detail: Phase 3. Task scoring weights are fixed: phaseGroup 0.3, dependency 0.4, trendResponse 0.3. When Plasticity lands, these become plastic connections that reshape with experience via dopamine signal. Projects that benefit from batching would strengthen phaseGroup weight; projects with deep dependency chains would strengthen dependency weight. Requires: Plasticity (#19).

phases.name: Phase 2: Fix the Senses
phases.description: Wave 4 (parallel): Inhibitor, Motor Cortex, Evaluation Rework. Wave 5: Consultation Rework (integrates all three + Thalamus briefings). Per-Sense Summaries (#26) absorbed into Phase 3 Hippocampus.

features.name: Inhibitor
features.description: Sense suppression — project-level and per-task. Writes InhibitedSense to WM (slot exists). Wave 4 — no Phase 2 dependencies.
features.notes: Two modes: (1) suppress() — LLM-based relevance evaluation at scope boundaries (project/phase/subphase/task), modulated by NE level and explore/exploit mode, enforces minimum active senses. Clears narrower scopes hierarchically before re-evaluating. (2) detectCollapse() — judges whether tension resolutions are genuine synthesis or capitulation, returns CollapseSignal as build-cycle gate input. Consumes InhibitionBriefing from Thalamus with full sense library + WM state. Owned by Brainstem, threaded through rhythm definitions.

features.name: Motor Cortex
features.description: Replace builder — premotor plans, primary produces, proprioception self-corrects. Consumes Thalamus builder briefings + PNS Intentions.
features.notes: MotorCortex class with three-phase execute(): premotor (callStructured → MotorPlan), primary motor (call → string with plan injected), proprioception (callStructured → SelfAssessment, modulated by checkpoint policy). Produces Intention[] from plan for Phase 3 learning systems. Backward-compat build() function preserved for deprecated orchestrator. Proprioception penalty applied in gate: low plan adherence penalizes effective min score by up to 2 points. RevisionPlan distinguishes execution-error (amend plan) from plan-error (re-plan from scratch).

features.name: Hippocampus
features.description: Episodic memory — full task stories, cross-project patterns
features.notes: Per-Sense Project Summaries (Feature #26) are the per-sense face of the Hippocampus + Crystallization, not a separate system. Each sense's 'running narrative' is crystallized understanding derived from its episodes. Implementation: (1) Episodes must capture per-sense participation — what each sense contributed (perspective, evaluations, tensions, resolutions) per task. (2) Crystallization must support per-sense scoping — crystallize Design's episodes into Design's narrative, separately from Performance's. (3) The Thalamus queries the Hippocampus per-sense and includes the crystallized summary in consultation briefings, giving each sense continuity across tasks. The sense doesn't own its summary — the Hippocampus stores it, crystallization produces it, the Thalamus routes it. Feature #26 is resolved by building this, not as a separate feature.

features.name: Crystallization
features.description: Hippocampus method — clusters episodes into principles
features.notes: Must support per-sense crystallization (see Hippocampus notes). Design's episodes crystallize into Design's narrative ('dark/bold established, image-heavy pages are risky'). This is the mechanism that produces Feature #26's per-sense project summaries. Triggers include: after each task (per-sense update), between-task consolidation (cross-sense), and the existing triggers (pattern density, surprise, contradiction).
